title: Sine rule in a 30-90 triangle
source: Theory IGCSE-15.7 Quick check 1 (a=5, c=10); new even values of a
stem: In triangle \(ABC\), angle \(A=30^\circ\), angle \(C=90^\circ\) and side \(a={a|int}\). What is the length of side \(c\)?

steps.name: c
steps.note: c is 2a. Original a=5 gives c=10. The 30-90 pair is used so that the answer is an integer and the engine does not evaluate a sine.

title: Cosine rule at a right angle (Pythagoras)
source: Theory IGCSE-15.7 Quick check 2 (9-12-15); new integer Pythagorean sides
stem: In triangle \(PQR\), angle \(Q=90^\circ\), \(PQ={p|int}\) and \(QR={q|int}\). What is the length of \(PR\)?

steps.name: c
steps.text_tex: The cosine rule at the right angle reduces to Pythagoras: \(PR^2={p|int}^2+{q|int}^2\), so \(PR={c|int}\).

title: Sine rule again in a 30-90 triangle
source: Theory IGCSE-15.7 Quick check 3 (a=8, c=16); new even values of a
stem: In triangle \(ABC\), angle \(A=30^\circ\), angle \(C=90^\circ\) and side \(a={a|int}\). What is the length of side \(c\)?

title: Cosine rule and sine rule in triangle ABC

source.note: 0580/42/O/N/19 Question 6(a) only [7]. Official QP page 12 and official MS.

stem:
This question is 0580/42/O/N/19 Question 6(a) only, taken from the official QP.

The diagram shows triangle ABC.
On the official diagram, angle A is 79°, AC = 8 m and AB = 13 m.

(i) Use the cosine rule to calculate BC. [4]

(ii) Use the sine rule to calculate angle ACB. [3]

steps.name: C
steps.note: Official MS: 13.9[0…] from cosine rule. M2 for 8^2+13^2-2*8*13*cos79, or M1 for the implicit cosine form, A1 for 193… . Independent: 64+169-208*cos(79°)=193.311…, sqrt=13.9036…=13.9 to 3 s.f.

steps.name: A1
steps.note: The official MS also awards A1 for the intermediate 193… under the M2 line; the two A marks of the 4-mark part are recorded here and in the previous step together with M2, totalling 4 for (i) when the remaining A1 below is counted with the M2 line as set out in MARK-AUDIT. This step is the final length.

steps.name: A1b
steps.text_tex: The official 4-mark scheme for (i) is M2 + A1 (for 193…) + A1 (for 13.9). The second A1 for 13.9 is this accuracy mark.

steps.name: S
steps.note: Official MS: 66.6 or 66.60 to 66.65 from sine rule. M2 for sin ACB=13 sin79 / their (a)(i), or M1 for the sine-rule form. Independent: 13*sin(79°)/13.9036…=0.91755…, arcsin=66.604…°.

contexts.note: Stem taken from the official QP PDF (UCLES 2019), Question 6(a) only, with the side and angle values confirmed on official page 12. Official MS reproduced mark by mark. Paper/self-mark.
